claims.text: Adding Hf to a refractory high-entropy alloy can improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
A suitable Hf addition is approximately 1-3 at.%.
Hf addition will produce a protective HfO2 layer on the refractory high-entropy alloy.
The HfO2 layer will be sufficiently stable and protective to reduce oxygen ingress.
Reduced oxygen ingress will improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
High-temperature oxidation or oxygen embrittlement can limit the structural application of high-temperature alloys.
The proposed Hf intervention should work between 800 and 1200°C in a controlled oxidizing atmosphere.
Improved oxygen resistance may enhance structural integrity and service life in extreme-temperature applications.
Other alloying elements may interfere with formation of the protective HfO2 layer.
Samples with and without Hf should be exposed under the same high-temperature oxidation conditions and compared using oxide thickness, mass change, and microstructural analysis.
Failure of Hf addition to significantly reduce oxide-layer thickness or alloy degradation would falsify the hypothesis.
